Fans look great and move a lot of air, with not so much sound to them (in my opinion). They've only gotten loud once I push them to max RPM, and even then you more-than-likely won't be bothered by them if you're wearing a headset or earbuds. The addressable RGB is subtle yet strong, although one minor issue I have with the lights is that the colors aren't exactly 'accurate' to the specific hexcode given which can throw your build's aesthetic off depending on the color(s) you pick.
Another problem, which can be more of a 'major' issue depending on the case you decide to build in, is that the fan screws that these come with have small heads—as in, small enough to go right through the holes of my case (Fractal Design Meshify 2 XL). Many times when putting these case fans on, I'd screw them on only for the screw to go straight into the fan itself, ignoring the case entirely (this would force me to take out ALL of the screws on the fan if there were others in, because trying to unscrew the one problematic screw would 'push' the fan away from the case while the other screws were still intact. Be careful not to bend your case!). All-in-all, you're more than likely better off sticking with the native fan screws that your case comes with.
In the end I'm still happy with this purchase, and I would recommend Arctic fans to others—with a slight degree of caution.

Cons: - Terrible price. Should NOT be almost $90, maybe $70 at most. - No daisy chaining for the PWM headers, the 3 Pin ARGB headers are daisy chainable (it comes with an ARGB hub?!?!?!) when my $14 have that ability, which is just outrageous - Audible. Not jet-turbine levels of noise, but they're definitely pretty loud. - ARGB hub that comes with it arrived broken with my set, wouldn't recognize any software and would freeze after a few seconds.
Overall, decent fans, as long as you can find them on sale and have a fan hub laying around.
